Thought: I'll examine the electron configuration of each element to determine which ones have valence electrons in both s and d-sublevels in the ground state.

B. Cr (Chromium): Atomic number 24

D. Mn (Manganese): Atomic number 25
Electron configuration: 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p⁶ 4s² 3d⁵
Valence electrons are in 4s and 3d sublevels, so it has electrons in both s and d.

E. Na (Sodium): Atomic number 11

F. Ni (Nickel): Atomic number 28
Electron configuration: 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p⁶ 4s² 3d⁸
Valence electrons are in 4s and 3d sublevels, so it has electrons in both s and d.

- Cr (Chromium)
